message.content: The 19th‑century sculpture that has become almost synonymous with the era itself is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**.  Created at the very end of the century, it captured the Romantic fascination with emotion, intimacy, and the human form, and it quickly became one of the most reproduced and celebrated works of the time.  While Rodin’s later “The Thinker” (1902) would eclipse it in fame, “The Kiss” remains the quintessential 19th‑century masterpiece that people still recognize today.
